study_type_evidence.quote: Male mice received a single i.p. injection of 1 nmol KP-10 or 1 nmol KP-54.

in_vivo_species.quote: 3–5 month old wild-type (129S6/SvEv) male mice were used in this study.

agents.name: KP-54 (human kisspeptin-54)
agents.sequence_source: Body states only that kisspeptins are amidated peptides of 54, 14, 13 or 10 amino acids sharing a common C-terminal decapeptide, and that human KP-54 was synthesized by the Advanced Biotechnology Centre; no sequence letters are printed.
agents.chemical_identifier: Human KP-54 synthesized by the Advanced Biotechnology Centre, Imperial College, London, UK
agents.group_n_quote: 100 μl of blood was collected from the lateral tail vein from groups of mice (n = 4) for each time point
agents.dose_route_quote: Male mice received a single i.p. injection of 1 nmol KP-10 or 1 nmol KP-54.
agents.cmax: 12292 ± 2655 pmol/l at 5 min (still 13193 ± 4364 pmol/L at 30 min)
agents.pk_quote: plasma KP-54 increased rapidly after injection and reached a maximum at 5 min (12292 ± 2655 pmol/l) that lasted until 30 min (13193 ± 4364 pmol/L). We calculated the half-life of plasma KP-54 to be around 32 min in the mouse

agents.name: KP-10 (human kisspeptin-10 / Metastin 45-54 amide)
agents.sequence_source: Body states only that KP-10 consists of the C-terminal 10 amino acids of KP-54 and that it is very hydrophobic with 5/10 aromatic or aliphatic residues; no sequence letters are printed.
agents.group_n_quote: 100 μl of blood was collected from the lateral tail vein from groups of mice (n = 4) for each time point
agents.dose: 1 nmol in 100 μl sterile PBS (also 10 nmol single dose, and 6 repeat injections of 1 nmol every 10 min, in the LH study only)
agents.dose_route_quote: Male mice received a single i.p. injection of 1 nmol KP-10 or 1 nmol KP-54.
agents.pk_quote: KP-10 peaked at 248 ± 9 pmol/l at 2 min post-injection and was undetectable by 10 min (Fig 4). We estimate that KP-10 has a plasma half-life of about 4 min

agents.name: PBS (vehicle control)
agents.chemical_identifier: 137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl, 10 mM Na2HPO4, 1.8 mM KH2PO4, pH 7.4
agents.group_n_quote: LH levels in adult male mice 10 min and 2 hrs after intraperitoneal injection of PBS (veh, n = 8), 1 nmol KP-10 (n = 8), or 1 nmol KP-54 (n = 8)
agents.dose_route_quote: Male mice received a single intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of 100 μl of PBS (vehicle control; 137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl

agents.name: KP-10 with a C-terminal penetratin sequence
agents.sequence_source: Body describes only the addition of a penetratin sequence to the C-terminal end of the decapeptide; no sequence letters are printed and the data are in supplementary S1 Fig.
agents.dose_route_quote: We attempted to facilitate greater permeability of KP-10 across the blood brain barrier (BBB) by adding a penetratin sequence to the C-terminal end

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Radioimmunoassay analysis of kisspeptin plasma levels over 2 hours after 1 nmole i.p. injection of KP-10 (n = 4) or KP-54 (n = 4).
concentration_time_figure.note: Plasma kisspeptin concentration (pmol/l) versus time over 2 h after a single 1 nmol i.p. dose, plotted separately for KP-10 and KP-54 on different y-axis scales; sampling at 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60 and 120 min.

bioanalytical_method: In-house competitive radioimmunoassay (RIA) using sheep polyclonal antibody GQ2 raised against human KP-54
bioanalytical_quote: Kisspeptin concentrations were measured using an established in house competitive radioimmunoassay (RIA,. Briefly, this RIA uses a sheep polyclonal antibody (GQ2)
notes: Both Cmax and tmax are reported in the body for both peptides: KP-10 248 ± 9 pmol/l at 2 min; KP-54 12292 ± 2655 pmol/l at 5 min. Half-lives are given as approximate values with no error terms and no named phase, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and both phase-specific fields are left 'not reported' - the paper does not fit or report a two-phase model. The authors caveat the KP-54 value: the RIA recognises all forms of kisspeptin, so the measured 32 min may partly reflect immunoreactive breakdown products; and they speculate that the apparent short half-life of KP-10 may reflect sequestration by serum proteins. Human KP-54 and KP-10 were used because the RIA does not detect mouse kisspeptins. The 3.8 min and 28 min human values quoted in the Discussion are literature comparisons, not measurements from this study, and are not recorded as agent values. Sequences are not printed in the body, so they are 'not reported' despite the PEPLIFE2 header listing them. BSA-FITC is a blood-brain-barrier tracer and dextrose-like challenge agents are not covered by the protocol role enum, so 'other' is used. Procedural agents (pentobarbital anaesthesia/euthanasia, paraformaldehyde perfusion) are not listed as tested substances.
